 Prayer:

This Writ petition has been filed under Article 226 of the  Constitution of India, praying to issue a Writ of Madamus after cal  for the records relating to the Award of the 1st respondent dated  07.06.2013 in I.D.No.255 of 2007, quash the portion of award, decli  to reinstate in service with continuity of service backwages to rei  the petitioner in service with continuity, backwages and other atte  1/8 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  W.P.N  benefits.
L.Ravikumar vs The Presiding Officer on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68314208/
1  For Petitioner : M/s.S.T.Varadarajulu  For Respondents : M/s.M.Chidambaram for R2  ORDER
This Writ Petition is filed against the second respondent, the Metropolitan Transport Corporation by the petitioner who was working as a Driver.
2. The facts in brief are that the petitioner has joined as a Driver with Staff No.D15296 on 02.09.1990 in the second respondent corporation.

On 20.07.2003, when the petitioner was driving a bus in route No.C.70, from Redhills to Guindy, at about 11.00 a.m., MMDA Colony, near Vinaygapuram Junction, a lorry came in the opposite direction and suddenly took U-turn and turned in the direction in which the petitioner was driving.
The petitioner applied brake and turned the vehicle towards left side to avoid colliding with the lorry.

The brake pedal came out and the bus did not stop and dashed against the left side body of the lorry and dashed against the hotel on the left side of the road, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and EB-Box and five pedestrians who thereby sustained injuries and died.
3. A charge memo was issued to the petitioner on 25.07.2003, alleging that the accident had occurred on account of his negligence.
The petitioner has submitted his explanation on 09.09.2003 and domestic enquiry was conducted and finally the petitioner was terminated from service on 02.05.2006.

4. The petitioner has raised Industrial Dispute in I.D.No.225 of 2007 and filed an application before the Labour Court/ first respondent seeking to set aside the dismissal order and to reinstate him back into service with full wages.
The said petition was allowed and award was passed on 07.06.2013 directing the second respondent to pay compensation of Rs.3,00,000/-.
However, the Tribunal has declined to order reinstatement with continuity of service and backwages and therefore sought for suitable directions.
5. Learned counsel for the second respondent has filed counter.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the second respondent and perused the materials available on record.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6.

There is no dispute that the petitioner who was working as a Driver in second respondent corporation with Staff I.D.No.15296 has driven the bus bearing the registration No.TN 01-N-2855 at 11.00 a.m., which resulted in death of five persons.
Domestic enquiry was initiated, petitioner was found guilty and terminated from service.

7. According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the accident has occurred not on account of rash and negligent act of the petitioner, but, it had occurred on account of mechanical failure,
thereby, he cannot be found fault, hence the termination of service on the ground that the petitioner L.Ravikumar vs The Presiding Officer on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68314208/
2 has negligently caused the accident cannot be accepted.

Learned counsel further submitted that the Tribunal should not have awarded compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- instead, the petitioner should have been reinstated back into service with full wages, arrears and consequential benefits.
8. The contention of the petitioner can be accepted to some extent.
Admittedly, the Criminal case registered against the petitioner in respect https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis of the accident in which five persons died, ended in acquittal.
Further, the family of the deceased have filed Original Petition before the concerned Tribunals, seeking compensation for the death of deceased persons in the accident.
In the said proceedings, the second respondent/corporation has filed detailed counter stating that the accident has not occurred, on account of the negligence of the Driver.
It was stated in the Motor Accident Tribunal by the second respondent Management that the accident has occurred due the mechanical failure of the vehicle.
A copy of the report of the Motor Vehicle Inspector was also not filed before this Court.

In any case, except the allegation that the petitioner/Driver is responsible for the accident causing death of five persons, there is no evidence on record to substantiate the allegation levelled against the petitioner.
On the contrary, the petitioner was acquitted in the Criminal case.
Therefore, on cumulative reading of all the above, it is clear that the petitioner cannot be found fault for the accident.
9. The Labour Court has also rightly concluded that the petitioner is not the reason for accident in which five persons have lost their lives.
However, having concluded so, the Labour Court instead of fixing the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis compensation should have ordered for reinstatement of the petitioner with backwages.
On careful perusal of the orders of the Tribunal, nothing is mentioned as to the reason why the compensation is ordered instead of reinstatement.
However as of now, the petitioner has attained the age of superannuation, therefore, he cannot be reinstated now.
What is left is, whether the compensation awarded is justified or not.

Is there any method following in awarding the compensation of Rs.3,00,000/-.
10.

It is reported by the learned counsel for the second respondent that petitioner's suspension period was revoked for some time and during that time petitioner was allowed to driven the passenger vehicle but again the petitioner caused the accident in which one person has died.
It is also reported that earlier also petitioner has caused many accidents for which the petitioner was warned.

In any case, though the past history of the petitioner cannot be taken into consideration for awarding the compensation, perhaps the Labour Court could have thought of track record of the petitioner and awarded compensation instead of reinstatement.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 11

. Insofar as compensation is concerned, according to the petitioner, a compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is very meagre, however, the petitioner has not mentioned as to what is just and fair compensation.
There is no record as to what was the salary that the petitioner likely to get in case, if he was reinstated into service.
Normally, once reinstation is ordered, only then the Court will consider for granting of backwages either fully or in part and not when compensation is awarded.

Since the petitioner was terminated from service in the year 2006 and the award was passed in the year 2013, this Court is of the opinion, compensation could have L.Ravikumar vs The Presiding Officer on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68314208/
3 been little more.

Considering the circumstances, though this Court is not in agreement with the submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner should have been reinstated and backwages should have been paid and considering the fact that the petitioner has attained the age of superannuation , this Court is of the opinion that the compensation Dr.D.NAGARJUN, J.
jai awarded can be raised from Rs.3,00,000/- to Rs.4,00,000/-, rest of the prayer sought by the petitioner are hereby declined.
In the result, the Writ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Petition is allowed in Part.
No costs.
